body: Marc Kulick's business partner in Vesta Realty has sued Kulick in Kansas, claiming he used the business for personal enrichment while hiding its true financial condition from investors, Oklahoma Watch reported on April 8, 2026. The 199-page complaint alleges that Kulick moved cash 'from entity to entity in a practice akin to check kiting,' ignored required accounting controls, and met investor information requests 'with blandishments, bluster and bullying.'

KJRH reported that the partner, who was responsible for raising capital, says Kulick was sole manager of the properties with exclusive control of the books, and that the partner wants Kulick removed from the company. According to KJRH, the suit alleges Kulick liquidated property without distributing proceeds to investors, took out loans without authorization and used company funds to pay at least $37 million in personal credit card payments, and it cites a forensic report calling his financial actions 'classic Ponzi-like.' Oklahoma Watch described the alleged diversions as hundreds of thousands of dollars.

Oklahoma Watch said it called and emailed Kulick and he did not respond. Vesta's chief operating officer told KJRH the company was aware of the filing and had 'nothing to share at this time.' In a July 2026 Bisnow report on a separate lender dispute, Kulick said he had operated in good faith. Vesta has promoted a portfolio of 39 multifamily properties with 9,975 units valued at $1 billion, according to an Oklahoma Magazine advertisement cited by Oklahoma Watch.

timeline.label: Oklahoma Watch reports on a business partner's 199-page suit against Marc Kulick filed in Kansas
